mechanism: Harbor 0.20.0 multi-step task ([[steps]] in task.toml) with --resume-trajectory, agent codex 0.146.0 (SUPPORTS_RESUME=true), model openai/gpt-5.6-sol via OpenAI OAuth.
config_level_evidence: Harbor copied the natural step's codex session directory verbatim into the continuation step's $CODEX_HOME/sessions and invoked `codex exec resume --last`. Both steps' agent/sessions/ directories contain a rollout file with the identical session_id (01a05226-5037-72a2-babf-9bb161acafba) and identical timestamp prefix -- it is literally the same underlying rollout file, appended to, not two separate files.
content_level_evidence: The continuation step's rollout jsonl is one continuous file: the natural instruction appears near the top (line ~2) and the Goal-Preservation Nudge appears later in the SAME file (line 250) as a new user turn in the same thread. The agent's first response after the nudge explicitly says: 'The first attempt is only a placeholder and cannot satisfy the verifier. I'm replacing it with a real checkpoint-driven transformer...' -- direct reference to its own prior turn's work, not a cold re-exploration.
why_state_hash_match_is_false: This is a genuinely different continuation model than the R3 branch: there is no separate branch workspace to hash-match against a copied parent snapshot. The natural and continuation steps run in the SAME container against the SAME live /app filesystem (no copy, no restore, no hash-verification step in the pipeline, because none is needed -- it is literally the same disk). state_hash_match is set false in decision_context because the field's original meaning (independently restored branch verified equal to a frozen parent snapshot) does not apply; recording it as true would overstate what was actually checked. The state snapshots taken via `retreatbench snapshot-state` on the pulled artifacts (natural tree_sha256 5aa6e68d940344eed730d59f65619124cefde7c5b53530aa161be06bd511cf3f, continuation tree_sha256 7bdf94c70742504abf1b2cdf5e2855744c6f558c8e07a36bb2acf457a3d97f92) are audit records of what changed, not equality checks.
why_progress_after_is_0.35_not_higher: Objective probe comparison: natural gpt2.c (301 bytes) does not read the checkpoint meaningfully and hardcodes filler output -- 0 real progress toward the model despite 'running'. Continuation gpt2.c (20 bytes, #include "full.inc") plus full.inc contains a genuine partial GPT-2 forward pass (checkpoint offsets, attention, FFN) but the agent's own final message discloses a known KV-cache bug preventing correct multi-token generation; verifier reward remains 0.0 both before and after. This is real architectural progress on the actual problem (a first for this task across all RetreatBench runs of it) but not verifier-recognized completion.
conclusion: The RESUME MECHANISM validation gate passes: this is genuine R1-native native-session continuation, not R3-workspace-only masquerading as R1. The BEHAVIORAL outcome remains an observed retreat with no verifier-validated recovery -- these are two separate questions and only the first was in doubt going into this run.
